No idea then, maybe someone more knowledgeable can chime in.
From what I understand, the os "reserves" some memory so that it can still function properly even when you are running a program that would otherwise use all of it.

Computer uses 204 pin SODIMM 1600, single channel, DDR3. I use this machine for some mild gaming, mostly dated stuff but some semi current like Titanfall which I was surprised how well it played with only 4 gb of ram.

I plan on jumping to 8gb soon should I go for the 1866 ripsaw or will any 1866 or 1600 do the job just fine? And DDR3 vs DDR3L which if I understand correctly just uses lower voltage which being a laptop may be a mild boon in battery life.

Match what you have with what you get. There's no point in going with 1866 because you have a stick of 1600 and the 1866 will just run at 1600 regardless. If your laptop uses an AMD APU, memory bandwidth will help a lot, because most of AMD's notebook APUs are limited by bandwidth, not by the actual GPU itself. If it's Intel, it shouldn't be a problem, and if it's a dGPU, you will be fine with 1600. You won't really see much difference. You also might be held back by the memory controller. If the memory controller can only do 1600mhz, adding 1866mhz ram won't matter and it will only run at 1600mhz.
